question: When converting a pretrained Transformer into a smaller sibling from the same model family, which cross-size structure is actually transferable, why do dense weight projections fail, and which initialization operations produce the fastest recovery under a matched continued-pretraining budget?

key_findings.claim: Cross-size similarity is much stronger in representations than in parameters, even when training data, tokenizer, and architecture family are held fixed.
key_findings.evidence: For Pythia-1.4B to Pythia-410M, per-layer ridge maps from 2,048- to 1,024-dimensional pooled activations explain mean held-out R2=0.844, while Procrustes reaches 0.717 and diagonal linear CKA averages 0.883. In the cleaner shared-vocabulary weight comparison, ridge explains only R2=0.248 for input embeddings and 0.386 for output embeddings.

key_findings.claim: A dense basis projection into the smaller shape destroys the Transformer's coordinate-bound computation rather than recovering a functional small model.
key_findings.evidence: Every target-free matrix projection has relative Frobenius error above 1 against the trained 410M target; even a target-aware shared fitted operator leaves 0.66-0.80 relative error. The assembled projection is confidently wrong on WikiText-103, while reconstructing the donor from extracted tensors reproduces logits with max absolute difference zero, isolating failure to basis mixing. The paper traces the breakage to fixed rotary pairs, head partitions, elementwise GELU, and diagonal LayerNorm parameters.

key_findings.claim: The residual left after the strongest shared linear cross-size operator contains no demonstrated layer-general or cross-pair correction signal.
key_findings.evidence: Residual effective ranks are 2.8-6.4% below shuffled and Gaussian controls, but cross-layer cosine is approximately zero. Linear and MLP-512 patch predictors reduce error by -0.0004 and -0.0003 on held-out layers and do not separate from shuffled labels (bootstrap p at least 0.99); transfer to 410M-to-160M is likewise null (p=1.00). A learned correction changes projected-model perplexity only about 2%, from 35,212 to 34,373, and remains nonfunctional.

key_findings.claim: Down-conversion initialization decomposes empirically into a function-preserving compensation lever and an optimizer-dynamics rescaling lever that operate best on different weight paths.
key_findings.evidence: Closed-form ridge compensation of the LayerNorm-free attention output and MLP down-projection improves subcloning zero-shot perplexity from 11,509 to 9,664 and 30M-token perplexity from 355.8 to 114.1. Variance rescaling worsens zero-shot quality as far as 61,912 but improves the endpoint to 86.4. Applying compensation to read-out paths and rescaling to LayerNorm-fronted read-in paths yields 18,459 zero-shot and 83.0 final perplexity, better than rescale-only on both axes in the initial run.

key_findings.claim: At a low 30M-token budget, the stacked initialization has a repeatable advantage over the paper's strongest subcloning-style baseline on the width-reduced primary pair.
key_findings.evidence: Across three matched data-draw seeds, HYBRID_RS reaches WikiText-103 perplexity 84.0+/-1.8 versus 89.7+/-3.7 for SUBCLONE_RS, wins all three paired comparisons, and has a worst seed of 86.0 below the baseline's best seed of 86.4. Relative to random initialization, the best transfer initialization is about 18 times better at 30M tokens.

key_findings.claim: The compensation advantage is primarily a low-budget token-efficiency effect, not a persistent asymptotic endpoint gain.
key_findings.evidence: At 100M tokens, the compensation-only hybrid reaches 62.3 perplexity versus subclone's 103.1 and crosses the latter endpoint after about 38M tokens. At 1B tokens, however, the two rescaled leaders tie exactly at 40.0, both ahead of from-scratch 57.4 but still well short of the pretrained 410M anchor near 15.6.

key_findings.claim: Transfer initialization generalizes to a depth-dominated pair, but the two-lever stack reverses at the largest donor scale tested.
key_findings.evidence: For 410M to 160M, three-seed 30M-token means are 113.2+/-4.5 for hybrid, 118.5+/-3.3 for subclone, and 1,505.2+/-57.9 from scratch; the full stack reaches 109.3 versus 117.9 and wins all three seeds. For 6.9B to 1.4B, however, rescale-only is best at 572, compensation-only is 776, the stack degrades to 1,213, and random is 1,413. The authors attribute the anti-synergy to an under-regularized 8,192-wide covariance solve, but that explanation is preliminary.

key_findings.claim: The initialization remains useful when knowledge distillation is added, although the comparison is small-scale and distillation does not help every initialization.
key_findings.evidence: At batch 16 and 30M tokens, HYBRID_RS scores 88.3 without and 83.2 with distillation, while SUBCLONE_RS scores 91.6 without and 96.7 with distillation. The teacher approximately halves throughput from 9.4k to 4.5k tokens/s; the conversion initialization reads the donor only once.

method.core_idea: Diagnose cross-size transfer at the levels of activations, weights, and residual structure, then construct the small model with architecture-respecting coordinate selection plus two path-specific corrections: least-squares reconstruction of linear read-out paths and variance-preserving scaling of normalized read-in paths.
method.mechanism: The study freezes 10,000 Pile sequences and compares Pythia siblings with CKA, Procrustes, ridge activation maps, and weight operators. It projects donor matrices with shared PCA/SVD bases, verifies extraction through bit-exact reconstruction, and tests post-operator residuals against shuffled/Gaussian controls and learned patch predictors. The constructive algorithm selects residual features by activation variance, rotary pairs by frequency matching, attention and MLP units by norm-based scores, and blocks by even stride. For a pruned linear read-out M and kept coordinates K, it solves M'=M Sigma_:,K (Sigma_K,K+lambda I)^-1; on the remaining LayerNorm-fronted input-cut paths it applies the subcloning variance factor. All training arms then share target shape, data order, optimizer, schedule, and token budget.
assumptions: Pythia siblings trained on identical data with one tokenizer isolate size sufficiently well to interpret cross-size differences as a conversion problem.
The frozen activation corpus estimates feature variance and second moments adequately for selection and compensation without target-model weights.
Whole-coordinate, whole-head, rotary-pair, and evenly strided block selection preserves the relevant architecture symmetries better than dense mixing.
Only attention-output and MLP-down paths have well-defined unnormalized linear reconstruction targets; compensation on normalized read-in paths is deliberately left open.
Matched token count and schedule are an adequate compute comparison, although teacher distillation changes throughput and the 100M/1B horizons use different schedules.
The implemented 'subcloning-style' baseline is close enough to Weight Subcloning for a controlled comparison despite different importance scores, block deletion, and rescaling treatment.
Low-budget recovery on Pythia predicts practical family expansion even though converted checkpoints remain far from full-pretraining quality.

techniques.role: Separates activation alignment from parameter alignment with held-out CKA, Procrustes, and ridge fits.
Rebuilds the donor from extracted tensors to rule out QKV assembly and normalization plumbing as causes of projected-model collapse.
Keeps architectural coordinates, heads, rotary pairs, MLP units, and blocks rather than mixing their semantics with dense bases.
Selects paired rotary coordinates at a stride matching the smaller frequency ladder.
Refits surviving columns of linear LayerNorm-free read-out maps using donor activation second moments.
Repairs optimizer-facing scale only on input-cut paths where a downstream normalization does not make the correction redundant or destructive.
Tests spectra, cross-layer directions, within-pair learnability, and cross-pair transfer against matched noise controls.
Compares initializations under identical data, optimizer, schedule, and token count and repeats decisive contrasts across seeds.

evaluations.setting: Pythia-1.4B to 410M representation alignment on frozen Pile activations
evaluations.result: Ridge activation R2=0.844, Procrustes R2=0.717, and diagonal CKA=0.883, versus embedding-weight ridge R2 of 0.248-0.386.
evaluations.baseline: Cross-size input and output embedding maps

evaluations.setting: Dense target-free projection of all six Transformer matrix types
evaluations.metric: Relative Frobenius error and zero-shot WikiText-103 perplexity
evaluations.result: All target-free errors exceed 1; target-aware shared fits remain 0.66-0.80, and projected models fail to beat random initialization under the primary assembly.
evaluations.baseline: Real 1.4B/410M anchors, random-init 410M, and target-aware fitted operators

evaluations.setting: Post-operator residual prediction on held-out layers and a held-out conversion pair
evaluations.metric: Error reduction versus zero, shuffled-control gap, and bootstrap p-value
evaluations.result: Linear and MLP predictors have negative reductions around -0.0003 to -0.0004 and p>=0.99 in-pair; cross-pair p=1.00.
evaluations.baseline: Layer-shuffled residual labels and predicting zero

evaluations.result: Compensation-only gives the best zero-shot 9,664; the stack gives 83.0 final versus rescale-only 86.4, bare subclone 355.8, dense projection 1,054.5, and random 1,519.0.
evaluations.baseline: Random, dense projection, bare subcloning, and single-lever variants

evaluations.metric: Final perplexity across three paired data-draw seeds
evaluations.result: HYBRID_RS is 84.0+/-1.8 versus SUBCLONE_RS 89.7+/-3.7 and wins 3/3 pairings.
Hybrid leads 62.3 to 103.1 at 100M; at 1B the rescaled leaders tie at 40.0, versus random 57.4 and pretrained anchor about 15.6.
evaluations.baseline: Subcloning, random initialization, and real Pythia-410M

evaluations.metric: Final perplexity at 30M tokens across three seeds
evaluations.result: Hybrid 113.2+/-4.5 and subclone 118.5+/-3.3 both beat random 1,505.2+/-57.9; the full stack reports 109.3 versus 117.9.
Rescale-only 572 beats compensation-only 776 and stack 1,213; all beat random 1,413.

evaluations.setting: Frozen-teacher distillation on the primary pair, 30M tokens, batch 16
evaluations.result: Stack plus distillation is best at 83.2; distilled subcloning degrades to 96.7, and teacher evaluation roughly halves tokens/s.
evaluations.baseline: Same initializations without distillation and random initialization

limitations: Author-stated: all conversions use one Pythia/GPT-NeoX family; RMSNorm, SwiGLU, grouped-query attention, and other wiring require a new safe-path analysis.
Author-stated: recovery uses only 0.01-0.3% of the original 300B-token pretraining budget, so the claims concern matched-budget recovery speed rather than final pretrained quality.
Author-stated: only decisive comparisons use three seeds; many ablation, scale, hardening, longer-horizon, and distillation cells are single-seed.
Author-stated: compensation is defined only for two LayerNorm-free read-out paths and does not repair deleted blocks or normalized read-in paths.
Author-stated: the largest-scale stack over-corrects; dimension-aware ridge and norm control are proposed but untested.

Reviewer-identified: the paper calls weight residuals 'noise' although their spectra differ systematically from controls; the stronger supported claim is that the tested predictors find no exploitable correction signal.

Reviewer-identified: the subcloning baseline is not a faithful reproduction of the cited method because scoring, depth removal, and rescale application differ, so method-level superiority should be read as superiority to this implementation.

Reviewer-identified: the exact cause of the 6.9B failure is inferred from conditioning and a preliminary small-donor control, not isolated through ridge sweeps, spectra, or compensated-weight norm ablations.
Reviewer-identified: token-matched comparisons do not fully equalize wall-clock compute when distillation requires a teacher forward, and cross-horizon results are schedule-confounded.
Reviewer-identified: downstream multiple-choice tasks remain near chance after 30M tokens, limiting evidence that faster perplexity recovery restores capabilities.
failure_modes: Dense projections mix rotary frequency pairs, attention heads, nonlinear MLP coordinates, and diagonal normalization features, producing a confidently wrong model even when the projection preserves global variance.
Blanket variance rescaling can destroy zero-shot calibration because normalization cancels or distorts its functional effect even while training dynamics improve.
Covariance compensation becomes ill-conditioned at large kept widths and can amplify low-variance directions enough to anti-synergize with rescaling.
Magnitude or activation-variance selection can discard low-norm but causally important units; the paper does not test gradient- or Hessian-scored selection.
Depth-dominated conversion removes entire transformations that a same-layer least-squares readout cannot reconstruct.
A donor and target with different tokenizers, data, attention layouts, activation functions, or normalization paths may not share the structural correspondence assumed by the selector.
A low-budget advantage can vanish at convergence, so extrapolating a 30M-token ranking to full pretraining may select an unnecessarily complex initialization.
Residual-prediction null results can be specific to the patch granularity and predictor classes tested rather than proving that no nonlinear or global correction exists.
reusable_insights: Test whether transfer lives in activations, parameters, or optimization state before designing a model-conversion operator.
Use an identity reconstruction through the complete extraction/assembly stack before attributing a converted model's failure to mathematics.
Respect the architecture's coordinate semantics: selection can preserve nonlinear and positional wiring that a statistically optimal dense basis destroys.
Separate function repair from optimizer-scale repair and apply them to disjoint paths whose normalization structure makes each operation well posed.
Evaluate model conversion as a recovery curve over tokens, not only zero-shot quality or one final checkpoint; the best start and best endpoint can be different methods.
Include shuffle, Gaussian, held-out-layer, and held-out-pair controls before interpreting structured residual spectra as learnable signal.
Stress an initialization across width reduction, depth reduction, absolute donor scale, long context, out-of-domain data, and distillation because each exposes a different boundary.
At high dimension, choose ridge strength from the covariance spectrum or explicitly cap compensated-weight norms rather than scaling only by an average diagonal magnitude.
open_questions: Can dimension- or spectrum-aware regularization make compensation and rescaling synergistic for donors above 6.9B?
How should compensation be formulated through RMSNorm/LayerNorm and gated SwiGLU paths without choosing an ill-defined pre-normalization target?
Can gradient, Hessian, or causal importance scores improve selection enough to retain low-magnitude but indispensable units?
What operator repairs deleted depth rather than only width, and how should a fixed target budget be split between retained width and retained blocks?
Do the low-budget token-efficiency gains persist in Llama-, Qwen-, and mixture-of-experts families and at full pretraining horizons?
Which global or equivariant predictor families, if any, can extract useful cross-size signal from residuals that patch predictors miss?
Can conversion quality be forecast cheaply from donor covariance conditioning, normalized-path topology, and reduction geometry before training the target?
How do the one-shot initialization and teacher-distillation objectives interact across larger token budgets and capability benchmarks?

competitive_landscape.title: Weight subcloning: direct initialization of transformers using larger pretrained ones
competitive_landscape.difference: Weight Subcloning ranks and copies donor neurons and removes blocks to initialize a smaller model, demonstrating roughly four-times faster training. This paper adds rotary-frequency matching, activation-moment least-squares compensation, path-specific rescaling, residual null tests, and budget/scale boundary studies, but its baseline changes the cited scoring and depth-removal recipe.

competitive_landscape.title: Sheared LLaMA: Accelerating Language Model Pre-training via Structured Pruning
competitive_landscape.difference: Sheared LLaMA learns target-shape structured pruning masks jointly with continued pretraining and dynamically reweights data domains. The present method uses the donor only at initialization, fixes the subsequent training recipe, and isolates selection, compensation, and rescaling rather than optimizing an end-to-end pruning pipeline.

competitive_landscape.title: Compact Language Models via Pruning and Knowledge Distillation
competitive_landscape.difference: Minitron combines multi-axis pruning, architecture search, and teacher distillation to derive 8B/4B models from 15B at production scale. This paper studies a cheaper one-use donor initialization in controlled Pythia pairs and shows complementarity with a small distillation run, but does not match Minitron's scale or training horizon.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning to Grow Pretrained Models for Efficient Transformer Training
competitive_landscape.difference: LiGO learns structured linear width/depth operators to grow a small pretrained model into a larger initialization. The present paper studies the reverse direction and argues that dense downward basis mixing is functionally destructive, favoring coordinate selection plus local reconstruction.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the new contribution is the controlled same-family characterization from cross-size representation alignment through dense-projection diagnosis and residual null tests, together with rotary-frequency-matched selection and a two-lever decomposition that stacks least-squares compensation with variance rescaling on different paths. The authors explicitly do not claim selection, least-squares pruning reconstruction, rescaling, representation similarity, or distillation individually. Reviewer inference: the most defensible novelty is the wiring-versus-blending diagnosis and path-specific experimental decomposition, plus unusually clear low-budget/convergence/scale boundaries. Superiority over Weight Subcloning itself is less secure because the implemented baseline differs materially from the original recipe, and the claim that residuals are literally noise is stronger than the evidence; the experiments establish a controlled predictive null for the tested residual representations.
reviewer_notes: Full text and appendices were checked through page 16. Quantitative claims were traced to the corresponding main or appendix tables. Author explanations are labeled as such where causal isolation is incomplete: especially the conditioning account of 6.9B over-correction and the interpretation of residuals as noise. Primary comparisons were independently checked on arXiv: Weight Subcloning 2312.09299, Sheared LLaMA 2310.06694, Minitron 2407.14679, and LiGO 2303.00980.
